bug_semantics: NLTK corpus-reader constructors accept an arbitrary caller-supplied `root` path and, before 3.10.3, `CorpusReader.__init__` converted a string root into a FileSystemPathPointer with no pathsec sandbox validation; reader bodies then read derived paths with raw `open()` / `sqlite3.connect()`. A caller who can choose the corpus root — LinThesaurusCorpusReader(root, ...) or PanLexLiteCorpusReader(root, ...) — makes NLTK enumerate and parse filesystem content and SQLite databases outside the pathsec data-root boundary (CWE-73), reading files the sandbox was designed to refuse.
flaw_origin: Commit cc344440f6e04fca7f472bad06dcad2eb1247d30 (2009-02-08, Steven Bird, "Changed: files->fileids ... issue 251") wrote the `CorpusReader.__init__` root-handling contract that the advisory names: `if isinstance(root, basestring): ... root = FileSystemPathPointer(root)` — converting any caller-supplied string into a filesystem pointer with zero containment validation. Every subsequent reader inherited it: LinThesaurusCorpusReader (created 2eabeab4114c, 2012-03-28, Dan Blanchard) reads its simN.lsp files with raw `open(path)` at construction, and PanLexLiteCorpusReader (created ab8305f6ca29, 2015-12-02, David Kamholz) runs `sqlite3.connect(os.path.join(root, 'db.sqlite'))` directly. The advisory's named sinks — unrestricted constructor roots reaching raw file/SQLite reads — are first fully assembled when pathsec existed as the sandbox boundary these constructors bypass; pathsec itself (4386e344d94c, 2026-03-17, Eric Kafe, ENFORCE=False default) validated only its own wrappers, and `CorpusReader.__init__` never called it. BIC anchored on cc344440f6e0 as the origin of the unvalidated string→PathPointer conversion that constitutes the bypass; reader commits are persistence waves.
